units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:1:25">Y. Ber. I, 2ᵈ</cite> top, v. <cite ref="M01939"><he>מָסַךְ</he> II</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sukkah 4:9">Succ. IV, 9</cite> <he>ולִמְנַסֵּךְ אומרים לו וכ׳</he> and they said to him who offered the libation (of water), raise thy hand.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sukkah 4:9">Ib.</cite> <he>שפעם אחת ני׳ אחד וכ׳</he> for once it happened, that a priest poured the libation out at his feet.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 62b:5">Snh. 62ᵇ</cite> <he>זיבח … וני׳ וכ׳</he> if one sacrificed, burnt incense, and offered a libation (to an idol) &c.; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:12:3">Cant. R. to IV, 12</cite> <he>מֵאָן היו ישראל מנטרים כל וכ׳</he> (read: <he>מְנַסְּכִים</he>, v. Matt. K. a. l.) whence did the Israelites take wine for their festive gatherings during the forty years &c.?

senses.gloss: to make wine forbidden (יֵין נֶסֶךְ) by the manipulation of a gentile suspected of dedicating it to idolatrous purposes.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 27a">Keth. 27ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Shabbat 41a:3">Sabb. 41ᵃ</cite> <he>אין פנאי לנַסֵּךְ</he> they do not take the time to manipulate the wine.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 56b:4">Ab. Zar. 56ᵇ</cite> (in Chald. dict.) <he>והא קא מנסך בידיה</he> but might he not dedicate it to idolatry by putting his hand into it?; <he>והא קא מנסך ברגל</he> might he not do it with his foot (while treading the wine)? <cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 5:4">Gitt. V, 4</cite> <he>המנסך</he> he who does damage to his neighbor by touching his wine for idolatrous purposes (v. interpret.
<cite ref="Gittin 52b">ib. 52ᵇ</cite>). Y. Ab. Zar. IV, 44ᵃ bot. <he>מנסך כל הבור</he> he causes all the wine in the pit to be forbidden; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be offered as libation, to be poured on the altar.
units: <cite ref="Pesachim 22a:9">Pes. 22ᵃ</cite> <he>כמים הנִיסָּסִין</he> like the water which is poured on the altar, opp. <he>הנשפכין</he> which is poured out at the foot of the altar.

senses.gloss: to be made forbidden (as dedicated to idolatry). Y. Ab. Zar. l. c. נתנ׳ הבור וכ׳ if the wine in the pit has been manipulated and become forbidden, the jet of wine poured into the pit becomes forbidden (affecting the wine in the vessel).
